Title: Black Cat
Comment:
Never liked the album much, besides this song. An early lesson against impulse buying!

Weird story: the music video for first song on the album, Rhythm Nation, used to cause certain laptops from ~2005 to crash -- not just if they were playing the song, but even if the song was played *near* them. The song is slightly sped up (pitched up) so contains a note that not many songs have, which happened to be one of the natural resonant frequencies of a particular 5400rpm laptop hard drive. A sound filter was added (to Windows or to a particular computer brand, depending on where you read the story..) to prevent the particular frequency from being played.

https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20220816-00/?p=106994
https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2022-38392

Title: I'm Sorry That I Got Fat (With The Wesley Willis Fiasco)
Comment:
Wesley Willis was a musician and visual artist in Chicago who developed a cult following in the early 90s. Most of his songs have the same 5 elements: 
- A keyboard automatic backing track.
- Spoken word.
- Singing the song title repeatedly, with a similar high-pitched yelled "melody" in every song - songs like "I Wupped Batman's Ass," "Rock n Roll McDonald's," "Chronic Schizophrenia" (he was diagnosed in 1989 before starting his music), "Birdman Kicked my Ass," and vulgar songs meant to repel hallucinated demons.
- Songs end with him saying, "Rock over London. Rock on Chicago."
- And a commercial motto (e.g., "Wheaties, breakfast of Champions").
But in this song, with the band The Wesley Willis Fiasco (instead of just a keyboard backing track), he doesn't yell/sing the song title, speaking/rapping it instead, plus he also drops the London & Chicago call-out and product motto, ending the song with a simple, "thank-you."
